# FERC Large Load Proceedings

> From DOE’s §403 ANOPR (RM26-4) to FERC’s June 18, 2026 show cause orders and the filings since

## What did the grid operators file on Nov 16?

PJM, MISO, CAISO and NYISO each filed large-load tariff rules under section 205 in new dockets, and PJM’s transmission owners filed the cost terms. Each says its filing answers its June order. PJM would study generators and large loads together in one 12-month process. MISO adds a project review with a $250,000 fee. CAISO offers interim service to flexible loads. NYISO offers firm and non-firm withdrawal service. SPP followed with three filings on Nov 18 and 19.

- [PJM](https://elibrary.ferc.gov/eLibrary/filelist?accession_number=20261116-5340#page=1) · [Page-cited positions](https://pranava0x0.github.io/ferc-large-load-proceedings/#filings/pjm-large-load/filing-er27-531-pjm-large-loads)
- [PJM transmission owners](https://elibrary.ferc.gov/eLibrary/filelist?accession_number=20261116-5300#page=1) · [Page-cited positions](https://pranava0x0.github.io/ferc-large-load-proceedings/#filings/pjm-tos-large-load/filing-er27-520-pjm-tos-large-loads)
- [MISO](https://elibrary.ferc.gov/eLibrary/filelist?accession_number=20261116-5323#page=1) · [Page-cited positions](https://pranava0x0.github.io/ferc-large-load-proceedings/#filings/miso-large-load/filing-er27-526-miso-large-loads)
- [CAISO](https://elibrary.ferc.gov/eLibrary/filelist?accession_number=20261116-5179#page=1) · [Page-cited positions](https://pranava0x0.github.io/ferc-large-load-proceedings/#filings/caiso-large-load/filing-er27-506-caiso-large-loads)
- [NYISO](https://elibrary.ferc.gov/eLibrary/filelist?accession_number=20261116-5282#page=1) · [Page-cited positions](https://pranava0x0.github.io/ferc-large-load-proceedings/#filings/nyiso-large-load/filing-er27-517-nyiso-large-loads)

## Questions in the filings

- [Who can see the registry?](https://pranava0x0.github.io/ferc-large-load-proceedings/reading/compliance-er26-3515-pjm/#read-schedule-11-b-1-b-d-validation-and-access) PJM would publish totals by distributor area where possible. Site-level filings stay subject to confidentiality rules. Ohio’s consumer advocate wants access under those same protections. [Source](https://elibrary.ferc.gov/eLibrary/filelist?accession_number=20261109-5209)
- [Who pays if a supplier leaves?](https://pranava0x0.github.io/ferc-large-load-proceedings/reading/refiling-er27-454-pjm-backstop/#read-ii-c-who-pays-if-an-entity-leaves-pjm) PJM proposes that the departing load-serving entity keep its backstop obligation. A later rate filing would set what it owes. The liability can outlast membership. [Source](https://elibrary.ferc.gov/eLibrary/filelist?accession_number=20261109-5216)
- [What counts as one site?](https://pranava0x0.github.io/ferc-large-load-proceedings/reading/compliance-er26-3515-pjm/#read-raa-article-1-what-counts-as-one-site) PJM’s 50 MW test uses cumulative peak demand. The clean tariff covers affiliated facilities within one mile under the configurations specified in the agreement. [Source](https://elibrary.ferc.gov/eLibrary/filelist?accession_number=20261109-5217)
- [Document reading room](https://pranava0x0.github.io/ferc-large-load-proceedings/reading/) · [Positions by issue](https://pranava0x0.github.io/ferc-large-load-proceedings/reading/positions.html) · [Machine-readable source inventory](https://pranava0x0.github.io/ferc-large-load-proceedings/reading/catalog.json)

- [PJM’s state commissions split differently on the two plans](https://pranava0x0.github.io/ferc-large-load-proceedings/reading/positions.html#state-commissions) Thirteen commissions backed OPSI’s August comments on the original backstop. West Virginia did not. Eleven backed its September comments on PJM’s registry and curtailment plan, including West Virginia. Kentucky, Ohio and Virginia abstained. Neither tally is a vote on the November filings. [OPSI, Aug 21](https://opsi.us/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/OPSI-ER26-3380-000-RBP-Comments.pdf#page=1) [OPSI, Sept 3](https://opsi.us/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/ER26-3515-000-IRAS-Comments.pdf#page=1)

On October 23, 2025, the Department of Energy invoked its rarely used § 403 authority to direct FERC to open a rulemaking on connecting large loads (data centers, AI, advanced manufacturing) to the interstate grid (Docket RM26-4-000), and asked for final action by April 30, 2026.
Rather than run a multi-year rulemaking, FERC answered on June 18, 2026 with six tailored § 206 show cause orders, one to each RTO/ISO. Each makes a threshold finding that the region’s tariff may be unjust and unreasonable for lack of clear, consistent large-load rules, then puts the market on a 30/60-day clock to defend the status quo or file a fix across the same five reform categories.
The through-line is cost causation made visible: the large load that triggers a network upgrade should bear its cost and spare ordinary ratepayers, with new transparency into how those costs are identified and allocated. The same morning, FERC issued Item E-2 (EL25-49-002), the order on rehearing that finalizes the rates and terms for the three new transmission services its PJM co-location proceeding created, the same services the six orders extend to every other region.
Where it stands on November 21, 2026: all six respondents have filed tariffs they say answer their orders, each in a new section 205 docket rather than the show cause docket. ISO-NE filed on Nov 13 in ER27-484-000 (comments due Dec 4). On Nov 16 PJM filed in ER27-531-000 and ER27-522-000, the PJM Transmission Owners in ER27-520-000, MISO in ER27-526-000 and ER27-527-000, CAISO in ER27-506-000 and NYISO in ER27-517-000. SPP filed last, on Nov 18 and 19, in ER27-559-000, ER27-577-000 and ER27-578-000; its letters also promise a response in EL26-68 itself on co-location rates, which was not on that docket’s sheet through Nov 20. Comments are due Dec 7 on CAISO’s, PJM’s ride-through (ER27-522) and MISO’s GRITS (ER27-527) filings; Dec 9 and 10 on SPP’s; Dec 14 on NYISO’s; Dec 16 on MISO’s ER27-526; and Jan 15, 2027 on PJM’s ER27-531 and the PJM Transmission Owners’ ER27-520. Valley Electric asked on Nov 13 to be dropped from CAISO’s order.
The Timeline tab holds the dated record: the August 3 and August 9 answer periods, the August 14 abeyance orders, the August 17 partial co-location compliance, the August 21 governance comments and backstop protests, and everything since. Each entry cites the document it was read from.

A static, independent analysis microsite (not affiliated with FERC or DOE). Source of truth: docs/js/data.js. Evidence is kept in three visibly distinct tiers: FERC primary, DOE primary, and secondary analysis.

## Key facts

- Authority: Federal Power Act § 206 · DOE Organization Act § 403
- Items and dockets: Items E-7 to E-12 · Dockets EL26-67-000 to EL26-72-000
- Reporter cites: 195 FERC ¶ 61,211 to 61,216
- Commission: Laura V. Swett (Chairman) · David Rosner · Lindsay S. See · Judy W. Chang · David LaCerte
- Order record as of 2026-06-22; Discourse commentary gathered through 2026-11-12
- RTOs / ISOs: 6, all FERC-jurisdictional grid operators + their TOs
- Reform categories: 5, teed up in each tailored order
- Informational report: 30 days, resource-adequacy plan to serve large loads
- Justify or file: 60 days, defend tariffs or propose §206 revisions; all six in abeyance to Nov 16 (SPP Nov 20)
- “Large load”: > 20 MW, DOE threshold (per Order No. 2003)
- Pages reviewed: 3,500+, public comments in the RM26-4 docket

## The six show cause orders (E-7 to E-12)

Each order PDF is committed and served at the page-precise link below; the official FERC source (Cloudflare-gated) is noted after it.

- [E-7 PJM, EL26-67-000, 195 FERC ¶ 61,211, 114 pp](https://pranava0x0.github.io/ferc-large-load-proceedings/orders/e-7-pjm-el26-67-000.pdf): Co-location rules already in place. Region: Mid-Atlantic / 13 states + DC. Official: https://www.ferc.gov/media/e-7-el26-67-000
- [E-8 MISO, EL26-70-000, 195 FERC ¶ 61,212, 115 pp](https://pranava0x0.github.io/ferc-large-load-proceedings/orders/e-8-miso-el26-70-000.pdf): Early-stage large-load rules. Region: 15 states, Midwest + South. Official: https://www.ferc.gov/media/e-8-el26-70-000
- [E-9 SPP, EL26-68-000, 195 FERC ¶ 61,213, 92 pp](https://pranava0x0.github.io/ferc-large-load-proceedings/orders/e-9-spp-el26-68-000.pdf): Most mature: HILL / HILLGA. Region: Central U.S., 14+ states. Official: https://www.ferc.gov/media/e-9-el26-68-000
- [E-10 CAISO, EL26-71-000, 195 FERC ¶ 61,214, 118 pp](https://pranava0x0.github.io/ferc-large-load-proceedings/orders/e-10-caiso-el26-71-000.pdf): No Order No. 888 service. Region: California (+ WEIM footprint). Official: https://www.ferc.gov/media/e-10-el26-71-000
- [E-11 ISO-NE, EL26-72-000, 195 FERC ¶ 61,215, 115 pp](https://pranava0x0.github.io/ferc-large-load-proceedings/orders/e-11-isone-el26-72-000.pdf): Transmission-constrained grid. Region: Six New England states. Official: https://www.ferc.gov/media/e11-el26-72-000
- [E-12 NYISO, EL26-69-000, 195 FERC ¶ 61,216, 119 pp](https://pranava0x0.github.io/ferc-large-load-proceedings/orders/e-12-nyiso-el26-69-000.pdf): Largely outside the tariff today. Region: New York State. Official: https://www.ferc.gov/media/e12-el26-69-000

## The PJM co-location rehearing order the six extend (Item E-2)

- [E-2 PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., EL25-49-002, 195 FERC ¶ 61,209, 278 pp](https://pranava0x0.github.io/ferc-large-load-proceedings/orders/e-2-pjm-el25-49-002.pdf): Order on rehearing, clarification, compliance & paper hearing on the December 18, 2025 PJM Co-Location Order (193 FERC ¶ 61,217), issued June 18, 2026. Finalizes PJM’s co-location services (Interim NITS, FCD, NFCD) — the services the six §206 orders extend. Official: https://www.ferc.gov/media/e-2-el25-49-002

## The five reform categories

- 1. Transmission Service to Eligible Customers on Behalf of Large Loads: Developing efficient transmission-service application and study processes, including consideration of alternative transmission technologies.
- 2. Cost Shifting Risk Among Transmission Customers: Preventing cost shifting and requiring transparency into transmission costs.
- 3. Co-Location Arrangements and Load with Behind the Meter Generation: Accommodating co-location agreements and behind-the-meter generation.
- 4. Extending New Transmission Services to Eligible Customers Taking Service on Behalf of Flexible Large Loads: Providing new transmission services for flexible large loads.
- 5. Interconnection Customers Serving Electrically Proximate Large Load and Co-Located Load: Developing a process to study generating facilities that serve electrically proximate large loads and co-located loads.

## Parallel proceedings (as of the 2026-11-21 news sweep)

### The six-market §206 clock (`sc6`)
- Venue: FERC Dockets EL26-67-000 to EL26-72-000
- What: Six show cause orders on one 60-day clock. Each RTO or ISO must defend its tariff or file a fix.
- Why it is tracked separately: This is the main proceeding the site tracks. The other lanes run beside it, each on its own clock.
- Status (2026-11-21): All six respondents have filed. ISO-NE filed Nov 13 in ER27-484 (comments due Dec 4). On Nov 16 PJM filed in ER27-531 and ER27-522, the PJM Transmission Owners in ER27-520, MISO and its transmission owners in ER27-526 and ER27-527, CAISO in ER27-506 (refiled as ER27-532) with fifteen California transmission owners in their own dockets, and NYISO in ER27-517 with the New York Transmission Owners and LS Power Grid New York. SPP filed last, two days before its Nov 20 deadline: transmission service and operating rules for High Impact Large Loads (ER27-559, Nov 18), a Load Safe Harbor Limit of $500,000 per MW with a $25 million cap on upgrade costs spread to all customers (ER27-577), and Price Adaptive Load Service, a non-firm service for loads that bid as dispatchable demand (ER27-578), both Nov 19. SPP asks FERC to read the three together with a response in EL26-68 itself, which its letters say covers transmission and ancillary service rates for co-located load. That response was not on the EL26-68 sheet through Nov 20. Every filing went to a new ER docket, and nothing new is on the six show cause sheets. PJM says it “has responded fully to the Large Load Show Cause Order” and asks FERC to close the section 206 side; the others ask much the same. FERC’s Nov 16 and Nov 18 notices set comment dates from Dec 7 to Jan 15, 2027; two Nov 18 errata notices moved NYISO’s ER27-517 to Dec 14 and the PJM Transmission Owners’ ER27-520 to Jan 15. Requests for more time are pending on MISO’s ER27-526 and three California transmission owners’ filings. NERC petitioned Nov 16 for large-load reliability standards (RD27-3).
- Next: 2026-12-04, Comments due on ISO-NE’s filing (ER27-484)
  - Dec 16, 2026: Answers due 30 days after the rescheduled responses
  - After the response records close: FERC decides whether to accept, modify, or impose a §206 remedy
  - Parallel lane: Rehearing and court-review risk runs alongside implementation

### PJM co-location: EL25-49 (`e2`)
- Venue: FERC Docket EL25-49 (Item E-2, order on rehearing)
- What: The PJM co-location proceeding that created the three new transmission services the six orders extend to every other region.
- Why it is tracked separately: A different docket with its own compliance clock, which has tracked the §206 clock closely: both were reset to Nov 16, 2026 on the same day, by separate FERC actions.
- Status (2026-11-21): PJM and the PJM Transmission Owners made their co-location compliance filings on Nov 16, inside their §205 filings. PJM’s ER27-531-000 refiles the compliance changes, including a 50 MW cap on netting retail behind-the-meter generation, and PJM moved the same day to withdraw its Aug 17 partial compliance filing. The transmission owners say ER27-520-000 also complies with the co-location order; its rates for the three new services largely repeat the ones FERC approved. Comments on both are due Jan 15, 2027: FERC’s Nov 18 notice set that date for ER27-531, and a Nov 18 errata notice moved ER27-520 from Dec 7 to match. The fight has also moved to court: Vistra Corp. (Oct 22, Case No. 26-3635) and Exelon Corp. and others (Oct 27) petitioned the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit for review of four orders in this proceeding, issued Dec 18, 2025, Feb 20, 2026, June 18, 2026 and Aug 20, 2026. That is known from the docket-sheet descriptions; the petitions were not read. No Commission order since the Aug 14 extension.
- Next: 2027-01-15, Comments due on PJM’s ER27-531 and the PJM Transmission Owners’ ER27-520
  - Oct 22 to 27, 2026: Vistra and Exelon take the co-location orders to the Third Circuit
  - Dec 7, 2026: Comments due on most of the Nov 16 filings
  - Jan 15, 2027: Comments due on PJM’s Fast Energization filing and the PJM Transmission Owners’ cost terms

### PJM governance: AD26-7 (`gov`)
- Venue: FERC Docket AD26-7-000 (Commission-led technical conference)
- What: A July 23 conference on who runs PJM: board independence, the stakeholder process, and the states’ role.
- Why it is tracked separately: Runs outside the §206 clock. Its September deadlines decide who controls PJM’s follow-through filings.
- Also known as: Also referred to in shorthand as the Swett technical conference, after the chairman who convened it.
- Status (2026-11-21): The Members Committee met Nov 18; no voting result for the governance package had been posted by Nov 21. Its agenda, posted Nov 11, says “The committee will be asked to approve/endorse the proposed OA, Tariff and RAA revisions as a package at this meeting.” The revisions put the term sheet the Members endorsed on Sept 30 into governing-document language: §205 rights over the energy-market schedules with a jump-ball rule for competing Member filings, 30 days’ notice of market-design filings, a permanent planning committee and an independence clause. PJM posted the redlines on Oct 13 and walked stakeholders through them on Oct 16. The states opposed the sheet. They wrote the Board on Sept 29 that if it passed they would “forcefully oppose it before the Commission and beyond.” Nothing says yet whether the Board will file the Members’ package, its own, or neither. Commissioner LaCerte told Utility Dive, in an interview published Nov 11, that PJM has “a stakeholder process there that has been proven to be detrimental to improvements in PJM” and that states should have “an appropriate-sized role in governance.” FERC has not acted on the Sept 30 vote. The AD26-7 sheet was read in full on Nov 15, and its newest row is PJM’s Oct 1 informational filing.
- Next: No dated step. Watch for the Nov 18 voting result and for what the Board files at FERC
  - Oct 16, 2026: PJM walks members through the tariff redlines for the Members' governance sheet
  - Nov 11, 2026: LaCerte says PJM’s stakeholder process has been “detrimental to improvements”
  - Nov 18, 2026: PJM’s Members Committee takes up the governance revisions

### The RM26-4 record (`rm264`)
- Venue: FERC Docket RM26-4-000 (the DOE §403 rulemaking)
- What: The rulemaking DOE’s §403 directive opened, and the 3,500-plus pages of comment the orders were built on.
- Why it is tracked separately: Still open. Everything the six orders left unaddressed stays live here, which is what the record-to-rule crosswalk tracks.
- Status (2026-10-19): Open with no dated next step, and nothing new on it since the June 18 orders. FERC answered the directive with the six §206 orders rather than a rule, and its Oct 15 open meeting agenda carried no RM26-4 item. The record's substance now moves through the regional §205 filings the orders invited; the crosswalk on the Comments tab tracks which of the record's issues each order reached.
- Next: No dated step
  - Oct 23, 2025: DOE issues a § 403 directive + enclosed ANOPR
  - Oct 23, 2025: Fourteen ANOPR principles define the reform menu
  - Late 2025 to Jan 2026: FERC opens RM26-4-000, takes comment, extends the period

### Market context (`context`)
- Venue: not a docket
- What: Auction results and market events that set the stakes for the filings, from outside any of the dockets.
- Why it is tracked separately: Mostly auction results and market events, kept in their own lane so the rail never reads an auction result as a docket event. PJM's backstop procurement (ER26-3380 and EL26-108) sits here too: it is a PJM market mechanism, not part of the large-load show cause clock, and its events name their docket.
- Status (2026-11-15): PJM moved on Nov 12 to withdraw its miscoded Oct 29 backstop filing in ER27-330. The same tariff records are pending in ER27-454-000. Comments on that filing and on PJM’s Nov 9 registry filing (ER26-3515-002) are due Nov 30. Two requests on the Oct 9 registry order are pending in ER26-3515-001: Ohio’s Consumers’ Counsel wants access to confidential registry data, and the PJM Industrial Customer Coalition and Steel Producers want limits on who sees it. In Exelon’s capacity-auction complaint (EL27-11), FERC gave PJM until Dec 21 to answer. In MISO’s joint-study docket (ER27-25), six consumer advocates asked on Nov 12 for conditions on acceptance. The backstop paper-hearing briefs are due Jan 11 and Jan 26, 2027.
- Next: 2026-11-30, Comments on PJM’s registry compliance filing and separate backstop refiling
  - Nov 30, 2026: Comments due on PJM’s backstop refiling and registry compliance filing
  - Dec 21, 2026: PJM’s answer and comments due on Exelon’s capacity-auction complaint
  - Jan 11, 2027: Backstop paper-hearing initial briefs, as extended

## Observed filings (checked 2026-11-21)

- Observed filings only. An empty cell means our checks found nothing, which is not proof nothing was filed. Every report and abeyance cell below is confirmed against its own eLibrary accession. Every abeyance motion was GRANTED on Aug 14, 2026, so the show-cause column is upcoming again, now against Nov 16 (Nov 20 for SPP) rather than Aug 17; each cell's gist carries the granting order's accession and reporter citation. A show-cause cell marked Signaled rests on the respondent's own written statement of what it will file (its source is cited in the cell), not on anything observed on the docket. Every show-cause response so far was filed in a new §205 docket, not in the show cause docket, and is marked Filed here because the respondent says it answers its order: ISO-NE on Nov 13 (ER27-484-000), and PJM, MISO, CAISO and NYISO on Nov 16. Their transmittal letters were read on Nov 17 and their docket sheets listed on Nov 18. SPP’s response is due Nov 20. Morongo’s Aug 12 answer in CAISO’s docket remains on file.
- Status vocabulary: `filed-verified` (eLibrary accession seen) · `filed-reported` (press or operator channel only) · `signaled` (announced intent). An absent row means our checks observed nothing, which is not proof nothing was filed.
- PJM (EL26-67-000), showcause, filed-verified, 2026-11-16: PJM filed under §205 in two new dockets: ER27-531-000, a 12-month Fast Energization Process studying generators and large loads together, three new transmission services, a 50 MW cap on netting behind-the-meter generation and refiled co-location compliance changes; and ER27-522-000, ride-through and operating requirements for large computational loads. PJM asks FERC to close the section 206 side of the order. The PJM Transmission Owners filed separately in ER27-520-000: rates for the new services, a cost recovery agreement with a minimum commitment of 80% to 100% of a firm-service benchmark, and a 15-year zonal allocation of Fast Energization upgrade costs. Accession: 20261116-5340.
- ISO-NE (EL26-72-000), showcause, filed-verified, 2026-11-13: ISO-NE, the NEPOOL Participants Committee and the transmission owners filed large-load tariff revisions under §205 in a new docket, ER27-484-000, and asked FERC to end the show cause case. Comments are due Dec 4. The EL26-72 sheet itself shows nothing new through Nov 15. Accession: 20261113-5007.
- MISO (EL26-70-000), showcause, filed-verified, 2026-11-16: MISO and its transmission owners filed under §205 in a new docket, ER27-526-000: a Large Load Project Review study process, two cost recovery agreements, a large-load dashboard and two new services, asking for a Feb 14, 2027 effective date and a 30-day comment period. A separate MISO filing, ER27-527-000, creates GRITS, a permanent firm and non-firm contract demand service that MISO says cannot start before Jan 1, 2029. MISO says these and its earlier LARS, zero-injection and reliability-requirements filings answer the show cause order. Accession: 20261116-5323.
- CAISO (EL26-71-000), showcause, filed-verified, 2026-11-16: CAISO filed under §205 in a new docket, ER27-506-000 (refiled the same day under a different filing code as ER27-532-000): a 50 MW large-load definition, disclosure of co-located load by generators and a Flexible Interim Load Interconnection service, effective Feb 16, 2027; comments are due Dec 7. Fifteen California transmission owners, among them SCE, PG&E and SDG&E, filed their own tariff revisions in separate dockets, where deposits, security and cost recovery sit; only CAISO’s letter was read. Earlier, on Aug 12, Morongo Transmission answered that its own tariff needs no change because it has no end-use customers (20260812-5158). Accession: 20261116-5179.
- SPP (EL26-68-000), showcause, filed-verified, 2026-11-18: SPP filed under §205 in three new dockets, two days before its Nov 20 deadline: High Impact Large Load transmission service and operating rules (ER27-559-000, Nov 18, effective Feb 16, 2027), a Load Safe Harbor Limit of $500,000 per MW with a $25 million cap on upgrade costs spread to all customers (ER27-577-000, Nov 19), and Price Adaptive Load Service, a non-firm dispatchable-demand service (ER27-578-000, Nov 19). It asks FERC to consider the three, together with a response in EL26-68 itself on co-location rates, as its response; that piece was not on the EL26-68 sheet through Nov 20. Comments are due Dec 9 and Dec 10. Accession: 20261118-5252.
- NYISO (EL26-69-000), showcause, filed-verified, 2026-11-16: NYISO filed under §205 in a new docket, ER27-517-000: Large Load Integration Procedures, Firm and Non-Firm Withdrawal Service instead of the three PJM-style services, and curtailment of non-firm service at a $200/MWh local price. It asks FERC to keep the show cause case in abeyance and end it for NYISO on acceptance. Comments are due Dec 7 under FERC’s notice; NYISO had asked for 28 days. The New York Transmission Owners (ER27-529-000) and LS Power Grid New York (ER27-518-000) filed cost recovery terms separately; those two were not read. Accession: 20261116-5282.
- PJM (EL26-67-000), report, filed-verified, 2026-07-20: PJM's informational filing on regional resource adequacy in compliance with the show-cause order. Accession: 20260720-5203.
- SPP (EL26-68-000), report, filed-verified, 2026-07-20: SPP's informational filing on regional resource adequacy in compliance with the show-cause order. Accession: 20260720-5205.
- NYISO (EL26-69-000), report, filed-verified, 2026-07-20: NYISO's informational filing on regional resource adequacy in compliance with the show-cause order. Accession: 20260720-5217.
- MISO (EL26-70-000), report, filed-verified, 2026-07-20: MISO's informational filing on regional resource adequacy in compliance with the show-cause order. Accession: 20260720-5204.
- CAISO (EL26-71-000), report, filed-verified, 2026-07-20: CAISO's informational filing on regional resource adequacy in compliance with the show-cause order. Accession: 20260720-5202.
- ISO-NE (EL26-72-000), report, filed-verified, 2026-07-20: Informational filing on regional resource adequacy. Outlines requiring new large loads to bring incremental new generation, and not procuring capacity for them through the regional capacity market. Accession: 20260720-5216.
- PJM (EL26-67-000), abeyance, filed-verified, 2026-07-28: PJM Interconnection moves to hold the proceeding in abeyance with a shortened answer period; the Indicated PJM Transmission Owners file a parallel motion the same day. Filed five days ahead of the deadline. FERC sets an answer period Jul 30 (20260730-3026); Constellation and the PJM Industrial Customer Coalition answer in support Aug 3. Granted Aug 14 (letter order 20260814-3059, 196 FERC ¶ 61,129), together with the Indicated PJM TOs' and Silver Run Electric's motions; responses reset to Nov 16, 2026. Accession: 20260728-5084.
- SPP (EL26-68-000), abeyance, filed-verified, 2026-08-03: Joint motion of Southwest Power Pool and other respondents to hold the proceeding in abeyance. Granted Aug 14 (letter order 20260814-3060, 196 FERC ¶ 61,128) for the 95 days the movants asked for rather than 90; responses reset to Nov 20, 2026, the latest of the six. Accession: 20260803-5209.
- NYISO (EL26-69-000), abeyance, filed-verified, 2026-08-03: NYISO moves for abeyance; the New York Transmission Owners (Con Edison, NYSEG, National Grid, O&R, RG&E, Central Hudson) and LS Power Grid New York / New York Transco file two further, separate abeyance motions the same day. All three motions granted Aug 14 (letter order 20260814-3068, 196 FERC ¶ 61,130); responses reset to Nov 16, 2026. Accession: 20260803-5229.
- MISO (EL26-70-000), abeyance, filed-verified, 2026-08-03: Joint motion of MISO and the MISO Transmission Owners to hold the proceeding in abeyance. Granted Aug 14 (letter order 20260814-3058, 196 FERC ¶ 61,133) over American Municipal Power's opposition, without AMP's proposed 20-day condition but with an express reminder that any preliminary finding the §205 filings leave unaddressed returns to the show cause proceeding; responses reset to Nov 16, 2026. Accession: 20260803-5249.
- CAISO (EL26-71-000), abeyance, filed-verified, 2026-08-03: CAISO moves for abeyance; a coalition of California transmission owners (SCE, SDG&E, PG&E and others) files a separate joint abeyance request the same day. The “Six Cities” (Anaheim, Azusa, Banning, Colton, Pasadena, Riverside) file a conditional abeyance motion, having already moved Jul 31 to rescind the order outright; the Western Area Power Administration separately moves to rescind as applied to itself. Granted Aug 14 by full order (20260814-3061, 196 FERC ¶ 61,131), which also granted the Six Cities' and WAPA's motions to rescind the order as against them under FPA §201(f) and amended the caption; responses reset to Nov 16, 2026. Accession: 20260803-5206.
- ISO-NE (EL26-72-000), abeyance, filed-verified, 2026-08-03: Joint motion of ISO New England and the Participating Transmission Owners Administrative Committee to hold the proceeding in abeyance, following through on the intent signaled Jun 29. Granted Aug 14 (letter order 20260814-3056, 196 FERC ¶ 61,132); responses reset to Nov 16, 2026. Accession: 20260803-5083.

## Commentary themes (secondary, in three dated waves)

- [wave 1, reaction to the June 18 orders, captured 2026-06-29] Cost responsibility is the center of gravity: Across the post-order discussion, the basic question is not whether large loads should connect faster; it is whether the tariff makes the beneficiary carry the cost and risk of the upgrade.
  - "There’s no real quarantining of the cost caused by data centers to those data centers" Source: https://insideclimatenews.org/news/18062026/federal-energy-regulatory-commission-data-center-orders/
  - "those loads bear the costs incurred to serve them" Source: https://www.linkedin.com/posts/jeffdennis77_ecaferclargeloadinterconnectionstatementpdf-activity-7473477334738599936-NWa-
  - "increasing scrutiny on who pays for transmission to connect data centers" Source: https://x.com/aniruddh_mohan/status/2069973894237184457
  - "President Trump's Ratepayer Protection Pledge" Source: https://www.energy.gov/articles/department-energy-applauds-fercs-action-large-load-interconnection-reform
- [wave 1, reaction to the June 18 orders, captured 2026-06-29] The regional route is both substance and litigation strategy: The six-order structure is being read as a deliberate alternative to one national template: faster than a rulemaking, more tailored to each market, and easier to defend.
  - "far more substantively ambitious than the ANOPR" Source: https://www.utilitydive.com/news/ferc-doe-data-center-interconnection/823360/
  - "six regional answers to the same question, decided on six different timelines" Source: https://www.utilitydive.com/news/ferc-doe-data-center-interconnection/823360/
  - "a much more robust and detailed administrative record" Source: https://news.bloomberglaw.com/environment-and-energy/energy-regulator-staves-off-critique-in-new-data-center-orders
  - "reduces future litigation entry points" Source: https://news.bloomberglaw.com/environment-and-energy/energy-regulator-staves-off-critique-in-new-data-center-orders
- [wave 1, reaction to the June 18 orders, captured 2026-06-29] Speed now depends on provable flexibility: The strongest pro-speed argument treats data centers as controllable loads, but the quotes also show the hard edge: flexibility has to be operational, measurable, and worth something in the tariff.
  - "emergency data-center load reduction ripe for deeper industry analysis" Source: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/demand-hereare-we-ready-build-briggs-white-cixae
  - "flexible AI data centers can adjust demand dynamically and act as grid assets, not only as fixed loads" Source: https://www.latitudemedia.com/news/catalyst-the-rise-of-flexible-data-centers/
  - "asset-backed flexible data centers can operate as grid assets" Source: https://www.volts.wtf/p/can-data-centers-be-good-grid-citizens
  - "paying other customers to shift load can be faster and more cost effective than curtailing expensive data-center chips" Source: https://www.eenews.net/articles/how-big-tech-learned-to-speak-ferc/
- [wave 1, reaction to the June 18 orders, captured 2026-06-29] Reliability and security remain live objections: The order is not landing as a pure acceleration story. Consumer and security voices are treating faster interconnection as acceptable only if modeling, operating standards, and stability protections keep up.
  - "security gaps remain" Source: https://x.com/BenSchifman/article/2067679572431138993
  - "data centers need any more help with interconnection to the grid" Source: https://x.com/Ben_Inskeep/status/2068025625860841880
  - "standards and rules in place that protect ratepayers from any negative stability, reliability and resiliency impacts" Source: https://x.com/Ben_Inskeep/status/2068025625860841880
- [wave 1, reaction to the June 18 orders, captured 2026-06-29] The physical buildout is bigger than the FERC clock: The discourse keeps returning to the same physical constraint: the orders can compress process, but turbines, transformers, generation, local consent, and deliverable capacity still decide which projects energize.
  - "power conversations for individual data centers have moved from megawatts to gigawatts" Source: https://cleanpower.org/blog/american-energy-american-ai-powering-a-secure-future/
  - "gas-turbine, transformer and interconnection lead times" Source: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/demand-hereare-we-ready-build-briggs-white-cixae
  - "power constraints and political resistance" Source: https://www.shanumathew.com/writing/data-centers-focus-on-energized-gw
  - "developers are pairing data-center growth with behind-the-meter generation and siting near stranded or underused power" Source: https://www.argusmedia.com/en/news-and-insights/latest-market-news/2804882-us-grid-overhaul-urgently-needed-to-meet-ai-load-ferc
- [wave 1, reaction to the June 18 orders, captured 2026-06-29] The organized-market focus leaves a Southeast gap: The order covers the six RTO/ISO markets, while several reactions flag the regions outside that structure as exactly where transmission planning and interconnection practice may be weakest.
  - "non-RTO areas, which typically suffer from the worst transmission and interconnection practices" Source: https://www.utilitydive.com/news/ferc-doe-data-center-interconnection/823360/
  - "The Southeast needs a modern transmission system" Source: https://ceba.org/southeast-energy-opportunities-require-a-bigger-better-faster-grid-business-leaders-call-for-regional-transmission-planning/
  - "we risk higher energy prices, power shortages, and lost economic opportunities" Source: https://ceba.org/southeast-energy-opportunities-require-a-bigger-better-faster-grid-business-leaders-call-for-regional-transmission-planning/
- [wave 1, reaction to the June 18 orders, captured 2026-10-20] The state line: FERC claims no new retail reach: On the day of the orders the state regulators' association reserved judgment on substance but welcomed the commissioners' nod to state authority. A law-firm read of the orders put the same point plainly: FERC stayed inside its existing jurisdiction and left retail questions with the states. By July, state consumer advocates were arguing that this was the problem; their case is in the summer lane.
  - "We appreciate the Commissioners’ comments at today’s meeting recognizing the critical role of states and state regulators given the jurisdictional division of duties under the Federal Power Act." Source: https://pubs.naruc.org/pub/A037DD09-A293-2927-B215-CD0CBE9FC0A4
  - "States remain committed to ensuring the appropriate allocation of costs across all customer classes and working constructively with our federal colleagues to that end." Source: https://pubs.naruc.org/pub/A037DD09-A293-2927-B215-CD0CBE9FC0A4
  - "Importantly, FERC did not assert any new or expanded jurisdiction over retail load or co-located load in a broad or preemptive sense." Source: https://www.hklaw.com/en/insights/publications/2026/06/ferc-advances-new-oversight-framework-for-large-loads
- [wave 2, the filings and the governance fight, captured 2026-07-28] PJM’s own legitimacy becomes the story: The July 23 technical conference took up how PJM makes decisions and set a September clock. The same commission running the §206 filings is now asking who gets to decide what PJM files, so this lane is a precondition for the other one.
  - "PJM is facing a grave legitimacy crisis" Source: https://www.utilitydive.com/news/ferc-pjm-governance-reforms-data-centers-capacity-market/826140/
  - "Some transmission owners are openly discussing leaving the RTO altogether" Source: https://www.utilitydive.com/news/ferc-pjm-governance-reforms-data-centers-capacity-market/826140/
  - "This is a cultural quagmire" Source: https://www.utilitydive.com/news/ferc-pjm-governance-reforms-data-centers-capacity-market/826140/
- [wave 2, the filings and the governance fight, captured 2026-07-28] Regional divergence: the tailoring thesis meets the record: The first observed answer to the 30-day reports points somewhere different from PJM’s expedited-new-entry posture. ISO-NE looks to new generation and away from its capacity market. That is the regional variation the six tailored orders were built to permit, showing up as substance rather than as a gap.
  - "requiring new large loads to bring incremental new generation" Source: https://isonewswire.com/2026/07/21/update-on-iso-ne-compliance-with-ferc-large-and-co-located-loads-order/
  - "not procuring capacity through the regional capacity market to serve these large loads" Source: https://isonewswire.com/2026/07/21/update-on-iso-ne-compliance-with-ferc-large-and-co-located-loads-order/
  - "intend to request a 90-day abeyance" Source: https://isonewswire.com/2026/06/29/iso-ne-provides-update-on-compliance-with-ferc-large-loads-order/
- [wave 2, the filings and the governance fight, captured 2026-07-28] Capacity scarcity is the arithmetic behind the argument: PJM’s 2028/2029 auction cleared at its cap for the third year running and still landed short of the reserve-margin target. Every claim about who should pay for new load is being made against that number.
  - "The price came in at the FERC-approved cap of $325/MW-day" Source: https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/about-pjm/newsroom/2026-releases/20260714-pjm-capacity-auction-procures-138318-mw-generation-resources.pdf
  - "short of PJM’s 20% installed reserve margin target by 6,831 MW" Source: https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/about-pjm/newsroom/2026-releases/20260714-pjm-capacity-auction-procures-138318-mw-generation-resources.pdf
- [wave 2, the filings and the governance fight, captured 2026-10-20] State advocates: transparency is not a remedy: On July 17 Maryland's People's Counsel, joined by the Ohio, Delaware and Illinois advocates, asked FERC to rehear the PJM order, and Pennsylvania's advocate filed separately. Their argument is that the order makes data-center transmission costs visible to states but leaves PJM's cost allocation in place, and states cannot move costs between transmission customers. Ari Peskoe of Harvard's Electricity Law Initiative sided with them. FERC dismissed every request on Sept 21 because the order had not decided anything yet.
  - "The order erroneously assumes State regulators have authority that they do not clearly have." Source: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MDOPC/bulletins/420fd48
  - "Each network upgrade added to a transmission owner’s revenue requirement while these questions remain open embeds another cost shift" Source: https://www.utilitydive.com/news/ferc-data-center-pjm-transmission-costs/825760/
  - "Unjust and unreasonable wholesale transmission cost shifts from large loads in PJM can manifest through unjust and unreasonable cost allocation of both [Regional Transmission Expansion Plan] projects and supplemental projects" Source: https://www.utilitydive.com/news/ferc-data-center-pjm-transmission-costs/825760/
  - "That move violates the law. PJM's Tariff guarantees cost shifts due to transmission for data centers. Only FERC can fix that. And it must." Source: https://x.com/AriPeskoe/status/2079226485626249625
  - "It did not order the utilities to charge those upgrade costs to data centers. They are still spread to everyone." Source: https://x.com/AriPeskoe/status/2080348438655295648
  - "We therefore dismiss the requests for rehearing, which concern a Commission action that is not final and that will be succeeded by further Commission action." Source: https://elibrary.ferc.gov/eLibrary/filelist?accession_number=20260921-3020
- [wave 3, October: the retail line, and the refilings, captured 2026-11-12] FERC draws the retail line under PJM's curtail-first service: The Oct 9 order on ER26-3515 is the first FERC ruling on large-load tariff text since June 18, and the ground it chose was jurisdiction rather than policy. The interim service fell because it reached retail customers; the definition and the registry survived because they do not. Analysts read the result as support for existing generators, and PJM's own reaction kept to cost causation.
  - "several provisions of the proposed Tariff appear to place obligations directly on Eligible New Large Loads, which are, for the most part, retail customers" Source: https://elibrary.ferc.gov/eLibrary/filelist?accession_number=20261009-3055
  - "the proposed compensation framework appears to establish a retail rate" Source: https://elibrary.ferc.gov/eLibrary/filelist?accession_number=20261009-3055
  - "we strongly encourage states to continue their important work on this issue" Source: https://elibrary.ferc.gov/eLibrary/filelist?accession_number=20261009-3055
  - "honoring the concept that existing electricity customers should not be unfairly burdened by new, energy intensive customers" Source: https://www.utilitydive.com/news/ferc-pjm-large-load-interconnection-iras-byonc/832716/
  - "the latest development is positive for existing generation/IPPs" Source: https://www.utilitydive.com/news/ferc-pjm-large-load-interconnection-iras-byonc/832716/
- [wave 3, October: the retail line, and the refilings, captured 2026-11-12] Rosner: curtail data centers last, and only after demand response: The one separate statement on the Oct 9 order. Commissioner Rosner agreed with rejecting the package and wrote to say what a refiled version would have to justify: forcing new large loads off the system before customers who volunteered for demand response, and excluding those loads from the capacity-market demand curve while the region sheds them involuntarily.
  - "That’s not only economically inefficient, but also likely to prevent supply and demand from coming back into balance." Source: https://elibrary.ferc.gov/eLibrary/filelist?accession_number=20261009-3055
  - "We need state regulators to establish clear rules for which customers should be curtailed first when circumstances require it." Source: https://elibrary.ferc.gov/eLibrary/filelist?accession_number=20261009-3055
  - "such measures should only be taken when necessary to keep the system reliable, after voluntary demand response resources have been exhausted" Source: https://elibrary.ferc.gov/eLibrary/filelist?accession_number=20261009-3055
  - "in an emergency, data centers not serving critical functions should be shut off before ordinary customers" Source: https://elibrary.ferc.gov/eLibrary/filelist?accession_number=20261009-3055
- [wave 3, October: the retail line, and the refilings, captured 2026-11-12] PJM answers two setbacks by refiling: After the Sept 29 backstop order and the Oct 9 large-load order, PJM's public posture is the same both times: review, then refile fast. Its Oct 22 consultation deck names Oct 29 for the new backstop filing and lists the fixes, including dropping the municipal and cooperative opt-out FERC said may be unduly discriminatory.
  - "PJM is reviewing the order and intends to work quickly to address the Commission’s remaining concerns." Source: https://insidelines.pjm.com/ferc-accepts-pjm-reliability-backstop-proposal/
  - "PJM submitted a motion for abeyance of the paper hearing on October 12 and notified FERC that it plans to submit a new 205 filing to FERC on October 29th" Source: https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/committees-groups/committees/mc/2026/20261022-special/item-01---1-tariff-section-92b-stakeholder-consultation-of-upcoming-205-filing-on-reliability-backstop-procurement---presentation.pdf
  - "Remove the opt out for muni/co-ops." Source: https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/committees-groups/committees/mc/2026/20261022-special/item-01---1-tariff-section-92b-stakeholder-consultation-of-upcoming-205-filing-on-reliability-backstop-procurement---presentation.pdf
- [wave 3, October: the retail line, and the refilings, captured 2026-11-12] Nov 16 is turning into a §205 date: Four weeks before the reset deadline, the respondents are saying in their own documents that they will file tariff changes rather than defend the status quo: the PJM transmission owners and ISO-NE in writing on Oct 9, MISO by filing pieces as it goes, PJM with a ride-through standard it says it will file in November.
  - "The PJM Transmission Owners have committed to submit their proposed revisions to address the concerns identified by the June 18, 2026 order issued in Docket No. EL26-67-000" Source: https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/committees-groups/committees/mc/2026/20261028/20261028-notice-of-pjm-transmission-owners-consultation-with-the-members-committee---informational-posting-only.pdf
  - "The ISO and the Participating Transmission Owners Administrative Committee (PTO AC) were granted an abeyance and will develop a Section 205 filing to be submitted by November 16, 2026." Source: https://www.iso-ne.com/static-assets/documents/100040/large_loads_integration_proposal_information_summary_10.09.26.pdf
  - "LARS provides MISO with a targeted tool to address the intersection of significant large load additions," Source: https://www.utilitydive.com/news/miso-large-load-generation-study-lars-ferc/832114/
  - "This type of operation is unsustainable and needs to be addressed," Source: https://insidelines.pjm.com/reliability-standards-to-manage-large-load-disconnection-events-proposed-by-pjm/
- [wave 3, October: the retail line, and the refilings, captured 2026-11-12] The backstop bill: who pays for capacity bought for new load: PJM's backstop buys capacity for a shortfall that large loads are driving, so the argument is over who carries the cost. Before FERC ruled, NRDC's Claire Lang-Ree read the proposal as PJM refusing to keep buying power for data centers, and Maryland People's Counsel David Lapp warned that households would pay if the forecast load never arrived. Two concurrences on the Sept 29 order answered: Chairman Swett faulted a filing made on the last possible day, and Commissioner See wrote that existing customers should not carry costs new demand causes. Ari Peskoe called FERC's cost-allocation objection surprising; DOE backed the order on Oct 9.
  - "PJM is saying very clearly to the data centers, 'We will no longer buy power on your behalf,'" Source: https://www.wypr.org/wypr-news/2026-08-26/pjm-looks-to-implement-key-data-center-regulations-maryland-energy-stakeholders-have-mixed-feelings
  - "If the data centers don't show up in those zones, then it'll be the existing customers, ordinary households included, that will pay those costs." Source: https://www.wypr.org/wypr-news/2026-08-26/pjm-looks-to-implement-key-data-center-regulations-maryland-energy-stakeholders-have-mixed-feelings
  - "This Commission will not be forced into accepting a deeply flawed, eleventh-hour procurement mechanism with billion-dollar implications for consumers." Source: https://elibrary.ferc.gov/eLibrary/filelist?accession_number=20260929-3099
  - "Existing customers should not be left paying costs attributable to new demand." Source: https://elibrary.ferc.gov/eLibrary/filelist?accession_number=20260929-3099
  - "Surprising! FERC has issues with the cost allocation framework that determined who pays for this data center capacity auction." Source: https://x.com/AriPeskoe/status/2105250742596784234
  - "the Energy Department supports having large electricity users pay for reliable new power generation" Source: https://www.energy.gov/articles/energy-department-supports-fercs-call-pjm-protect-ratepayers-and-build-more-reliable-power
- [wave 3, October: the retail line, and the refilings, captured 2026-11-12] After Oct 9, the states hold the pen on curtailment: FERC rejected PJM's curtail-first service as a reach into retail jurisdiction, and the reactions agree on the consequence: the next move belongs to the states. Jeff Dennis read the order as more pressure on them. Mary Yang, a former PJM regulatory counsel now at 804 Advisory, said it slows bring-your-own-capacity deals. NRDC wants PJM to refile with a bring-your-own-supply rule. And in a Duke Energy Carolinas order the same day, outside the RTOs, Commissioner Rosner wrote that FERC may have to widen the show cause orders' cost-recovery framework if state action falls short.
  - "In doing so, it appears to be putting more pressure on states to find answers." Source: https://x.com/EnergyLawJeff/status/2109669734568304766
  - "It does slow down the development of these more innovative bilateral mechanisms to solve some of these problems" Source: https://www.latitudemedia.com/news/ferc-rejected-pjms-data-center-curtailment-plan-whats-next-for-byoc/
  - "At a minimum, PJM's rules must require data centers to bring their own supply, and not allow them to raise electricity costs or cause blackouts" Source: https://www.bisnow.com/news/national/data-center-power/federal-regulators-reject-power-cuts-to-data-centers-that-dont-bring-their-own
  - "To the extent state regulatory actions are not sufficient to protect consumers, the Commission has an obligation to seriously consider expanding the cost recovery framework it established in the Large Load Show Cause Orders" Source: https://elibrary.ferc.gov/eLibrary/search
- [wave 3, October: the retail line, and the refilings, captured 2026-11-12] The backstop comes back, and the rehearing requests hedge: PJM refiled the backstop on the last day FERC's Sept 29 order allowed, as a new §205 filing rather than a brief in the paper hearing, and says it has answered all three issues FERC set for hearing. The same day, seven parties had requests for rehearing or clarification of the Sept 29 order on file. Consumer advocates from five jurisdictions want the market-power and price-cap terms fixed in whatever PJM files next; the Indicated PJM Transmission Owners said outright that they hope the refiling makes their request moot.
  - "PJM filed an amended proposal to FERC with the goal of commencing a Reliability Backstop Procurement on March 1, 2027." Source: https://insidelines.pjm.com/pjm-files-amended-reliability-backstop-proposal/
  - "Through this section 205 filing, PJM has addressed the issues set for paper hearing in the September 29 Order." Source: https://elibrary.ferc.gov/eLibrary/search
  - "permits the unmitigated exercise of seller-side market power" Source: https://elibrary.ferc.gov/eLibrary/search
  - "submit a revised section 205 filing that supersedes its earlier section 205 filing and may moot the need for rehearing of the Order" Source: https://elibrary.ferc.gov/eLibrary/search
- [wave 3, October: the retail line, and the refilings, captured 2026-11-12] CAISO's board signs off, and PJM books its consultation: Two of the six respondents moved on Nov 16 in the last days of October. CAISO's Board advanced the Large Loads proposal and its chief executive described the filing as the show cause response. PJM skipped the Oct 28 advisory vote the abeyance order had recorded and put a Nov 5 consultation on the calendar for several §205 filings rather than one.
  - "Our response to the FERC order to show cause will improve planning and operational awareness of new large loads on the system, prevent cost-shifting, encourage flexibility and expedite large load energization" Source: https://www.publicpower.org/periodical/article/caiso-board-advances-new-procedures-connecting-large-loads
  - "We look forward to our ongoing collaboration with our participating transmission owners, state energy agencies and industry stakeholders to make sure we stay ahead of the curve on interconnecting large loads without compromising reliability or placing an undue burden on consumers" Source: https://www.publicpower.org/periodical/article/caiso-board-advances-new-procedures-connecting-large-loads
  - "PJM staff will consult with stakeholders on plans to submit a suite of section 205 filings to address Tariff revisions to address opportunities identified in the Large Load Show Cause Order and related reforms." Source: https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/committees-groups/committees/mc/2026/20261105-special/agenda.pdf
- [wave 3, October: the retail line, and the refilings, captured 2026-11-12] MISO's fast lane for large loads splits its own footprint: MISO's Large Load Addition Resource Study would let new generation for large loads move ahead of the ordinary queue. On the Oct 23 comment date the states' committee asked for safeguards for everyone already waiting, Google said the design lacks protection against shifting costs to other customers, and the Data Center Coalition, while generally supportive, objected that utilities would decide which projects get in. The quotes are from the filings as Utility Dive printed them.
  - "LARS cannot become a general alternative to the existing [generation interconnection queue] or provide preferential access to transmission capacity without adequate safeguards for existing queue participants and transmission customers" Source: https://www.utilitydive.com/news/miso-large-load-lars-ferc-google-oms/849887/
  - "The lack of cost shifting protections is especially concerning because, despite the benefits — especially speed to power — that LARS would promote, it is structured in a way that threatens Google’s ability to meet its foundational commitment to ensuring that other retail customers do not bear the costs of serving its data centers, including through the Ratepayer Protection Pledge" Source: https://www.utilitydive.com/news/miso-large-load-lars-ferc-google-oms/849887/
  - "In MISO’s primarily vertically integrated footprint, establishing the LSE as the sole LARS application facilitator narrows the pool of supply that can gain access to expedited Large Load Generation Interconnection Agreements ... to only those projects that are effectively approved by the LSE" Source: https://www.utilitydive.com/news/miso-large-load-lars-ferc-google-oms/849887/
- [wave 3, October: the retail line, and the refilings, captured 2026-11-12] The customers ask PJM not to answer with a queue overhaul: The show cause order exists to get large loads connected faster, and the large loads are now arguing PJM's answer would slow them down. PJM told FERC in October that it will file a unified study of large loads and generation by Nov 16. The energy buyers and data-center operators who would use it wrote to PJM's Board on Oct 2 that a combined cluster with an annual cutoff could mean nearly two years between transmission owner approval and the end of PJM's study, and that MISO and SPP generally run load and generation planning in parallel instead.
  - "While the Order calls for improvements to large load integration, it does not require PJM to overhaul its entire generation interconnection queue." Source: https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/about-pjm/who-we-are/public-disclosures/2026/20261005-ceba-dcc-letter-to-pjm-board-re-ll-show-cause-response.pdf
  - "PJM has not demonstrated that this proposal will deliver the speed, certainty, or transparency envisioned by the Show Cause Order." Source: https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/about-pjm/who-we-are/public-disclosures/2026/20261005-ceba-dcc-letter-to-pjm-board-re-ll-show-cause-response.pdf
- [wave 3, October: the retail line, and the refilings, captured 2026-11-12] Bring your own power, as a presidential line: The idea that large loads should supply their own electricity has run through this record since June, from consumer advocates to PJM's backstop. On Oct 21 the President stated it as a mandate, with no docket or instrument attached, and the same day a Maryland senator, in a post of his own, put FERC alongside the White House as the problem.
  - "New and large, in some cases gigantic, Data Centers are mandated by me to make their own electricity, and give or sell any excess back to the local community, or grid" Source: https://www.bisnow.com/news/national/data-center-community-relations/trump-data-centers-mandated-to-supply-own-electricity-should-pay-dividend-to-communities
  - "When push comes to shove, Trump would rather you lose power than the data center companies lose a cent of profit." Source: https://x.com/ChrisVanHollen/status/2112897141727232399
- [wave 3, October: the retail line, and the refilings, captured 2026-11-12] After the midterms: who pays, and a guardrail removed: Commentary in the week after the Nov 3 elections ties the large-load record to voters. Latitude Intelligence's Nick Zenkin said the election changes the question from speed of connection to who pays. Ascend Analytics analysts said FERC's rejection of PJM's interim service removed a protection for PJM and that no one will tolerate paying new-entry prices to everyone, and reporter Maeve Allsup wrote that the Oct 9 ruling moved curtailment decisions to the states. ICF's Maria Scheller read PJM's refiled backstop as lowering risk for default-service utilities but leaving the question of state recovery open. None of these voices is a party to the show cause dockets.
  - "I think overall this changes the story from 'how fast we can connect?' to 'who pays?'" Source: https://www.latitudemedia.com/news/voters-just-proved-how-much-they-hate-data-centers/
  - "There’s no world in which there’s political will or political tolerance for new entry prices to get paid to everybody." Source: https://www.latitudemedia.com/news/what-the-midterms-mean-for-data-center-developers-in-pjm/
  - "IRAS was a guardrail for PJM, and that guardrail is now off the table," Source: https://www.latitudemedia.com/news/what-the-midterms-mean-for-data-center-developers-in-pjm/
  - "The ruling shifted responsibility for determining which types of new loads should face curtailment instead to the states." Source: https://www.latitudemedia.com/news/what-the-midterms-mean-for-data-center-developers-in-pjm/
  - "The key credit question is whether state rules provide timely, certain recovery and adequate customer security." Source: https://www.utilitydive.com/news/pjm-revised-data-center-backstop-procurement-ferc/873551/

## The RM26-4 public comments (corpus)

- 273 public comments (of 423 total eLibrary filings) on the DOE ANOPR (Docket RM26-4-000) were scraped from FERC eLibrary. Each text-extracted comment carries a quote-centric, auditable summary built the PNNL "CommentNEPA" way: verbatim quotes pulled from the filing, binned to the five reform principles / eight ANOPR questions / six regions (plus emergent topics), each bin with the filer's stance. AI-generated and provisional (not yet human-verified).
- Per-comment summaries: `sources/comments/summaries-v2/<accession>.json`. Compiled for the site: `docs/js/comments-data.js` (`window.FERC_COMMENTS`). Method + schema: `sources/comments/summarization-spec.md`. Explore on the Comments tab (a stance map + per-comment audited analysis).
